faq.q: How do I even apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your bank's ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount) facility via net banking, or through your stockbroker's online platform. Your money remains blocked in your account until allotment.
A lot size is the minimum number of shares you must apply for in an IPO. You cannot apply for fewer shares than the specified lot size.

**Mainboard** IPOs are for larger, more established companies and list on the main platforms of stock exchanges like NSE and BSE. **SME** (Small and Medium Enterprises) IPOs are for smaller companies and list on dedicated SME platforms of the exchanges, often with different trading rules and investor categories.

faq.q: Can I sell my shares immediately after listing?
faq.a: Yes, once your allotted shares are listed on the stock exchange, you can buy or sell them like any other stock in the secondary market, subject to market conditions.

faq.q: What happens if I don't get an allotment?
faq.a: If you don't get any shares in an IPO, the money that was blocked in your bank account (via ASBA) is simply unblocked and becomes available to you again, usually within a few days after the allotment process.
